clue.text: Grieved, provoked as otter suffered

parts.note: to be provoked or stirred is to be moved

indicators.note: the words as otter suffer, being knocked out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is upset because a provoked otter was hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffered' rearranges AS OTTER into TO TEARS, which follows MOVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being brought to the point of weeping is what it means to be deeply saddened or grieved.

clue.text: Disease caught in time as lesson unravels

indicators.note: the letters are caught inside the run of words time as lesson

explanation.surface: An illness is picked up during the period when the lesson falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in' points to letters running across 'time as lesson'; 'unravels' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Measles is an infectious viral illness marked by a red rash, so it is a disease.

clue.text: Cunning lulu getting up half hidden against tree

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
half of the word lulu is kept, the other half hidden away

parts.note: a pine is a kind of tree

explanation.surface: A crafty lulu climbs a tree and half disappears from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half hidden' keeps the first half of the name, and 'getting up' turns that half round, as a down clue reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a fox, the animal famed for cunning, so it means crafty or sly.

clue.text: Not dare to replace explosive device

indicators.note: to replace the letters of not dare to is to put them back in another order

explanation.surface: Someone lacks the nerve to swap out a bomb's trigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replace' rearranges NOT DARE TO into the nine letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is the small charge or mechanism that sets off a bomb, so an explosive device.

clue.text: Ring cliff for award

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
a scar is a steep rocky cliff face

explanation.surface: A ring and a cliff are offered as a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The statuette given each year by the Hollywood film academy is a famous prize.

clue.text: Egghead had hint about biblical king in poem

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of egg is E

indicators.note: about means the hint word goes round the king

parts.note: a clue is a hint
Og was the king of Bashan in the Bible

explanation.surface: A clever person dropped a hint about a king from the Bible in some verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' means an intellectual but here gives only the first letter of 'egg'; Og is a king from the Book of Numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pastoral piece of verse, such as Virgil's, is a kind of poem.

clue.text: Batter section of fortification

parts.note: to ram is to batter or strike hard
a part is a section

explanation.surface: Someone pounds away at one part of a castle's defences.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad defensive wall of earth or stone around a fort is part of its fortification.

clue.text: Flame gamely held?

parts.note: read gamely as relating to the Games: a flame carried and held aloft for the great international sporting contest

explanation.surface: A fire is bravely kept going.
explanation.definitionFit: The torch carried in relay to light the cauldron at the Games is a flame held for those games.

clue.text: Felt ale could have been removed from the sheet

indicators.note: the words felt ale could be moved about into a different order

explanation.surface: Beer stains on felt might have been wiped off the sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could have been removed' is read as re-moved, signalling a rearrangement of FELT ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a single printed sheet of paper handed out to people.

clue.text: Ring, ring me inside for some medicine

indicators.note: the second ring and me go inside the phone call word

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be phoned again so they can get some medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses of 'ring' differ: first a phone call, then the round shape of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Calomel, mercurous chloride, was once widely used as a purgative drug, so it is a medicine.

clue.text: Modest punter improved slightly

explanation.surface: A gambler of small means has got a bit better.
explanation.definitionFit: A modest gambler is a small bettor; and a condition improved only a little has got slightly better.

clue.text: Plant, one taking on very large number

parts.note: a mill is a factory or industrial plant
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A factory takes on one more worker, making a big number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a living thing but is a factory, a mill.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand thousands is an extremely big number.

clue.text: On the throne expecting to be decapitated?

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, comes off

parts.note: a woman expecting a baby is pregnant

explanation.surface: A queen expecting a child faces having her head cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be decapitated' removes the first letter of PREGNANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, so a monarch on the throne is regnant.

clue.text: Number of children?

explanation.surface: A question about how many offspring someone has.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine's numbered edition is called an issue; and in legal language offspring are a person's issue.

clue.text: Inflict pain before I left plant

indicators.note: before puts the pain word ahead of the rest

parts.note: to torment is to inflict pain

explanation.surface: Someone hurts others before leaving a plant behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormentil is a small yellow-flowered herb of the rose family, a wild plant.

clue.text: Rosalind on open land in Ireland

parts.note: Ros is a short form of the name Rosalind
something common is open to everyone

explanation.surface: A woman called Rosalind is out on open ground in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; ROSCOMMON is a county in the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Roscommon is a county, a stretch of land, in the Republic's province of Connacht.

clue.text: Word-list contained the south African wild ox

parts.note: A is a short form for African
the urus, or aurochs, was a wild ox

explanation.surface: A vocabulary list included an entry for a wild ox from South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a book listing words grouped with their synonyms, a kind of word list.

clue.text: Mob rage out of control because of the ban

indicators.note: the letters of mob rage run out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: A riotous mob reacts angrily to a prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official order forbidding trade, so it is a ban.

clue.text: One might buy a lot at it

definitions.text: One might buy a lot at it

parts.words: One might buy a lot at it
parts.note: read lot as a numbered item put up for bids, rather than a large amount

explanation.surface: A place where a shopper spends heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Items sold to the highest bidder are offered as numbered lots at this kind of sale.

clue.text: Beat broth that has been cooked

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of broth have been worked up into a new order

explanation.surface: A soup that has been simmered is given a good stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a regular beat or pulse, as of the heart.

clue.text: The alternative hum came from lute

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
BO, body odour, is a bad smell, as is a hum in British slang

explanation.surface: A different droning sound came out of a stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hum' looks like a sound but is British slang for a smell, hence BO.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorbo is a large bass member of the lute family, used in baroque music.

clue.text: Later is represented by pragmatist

indicators.note: the letters of later is are presented again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A practical person is shown by what comes afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist deals with things as they actually are, which is what a practical, pragmatic person does.

clue.text: Lady be about first with hundreds then one more

indicators.note: first puts the about word at the front

parts.note: re means about, concerning
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so CC is hundreds
A means one

explanation.surface: A woman is asked to be concerned, first with hundreds and then one more.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is a woman's first name, so it can stand for a lady.

clue.text: Small part, in motoring organisation, of main arterial way

indicators.note: in puts the small part inside the motoring body

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is a British motoring organisation
an ort is a scrap or small leftover piece

explanation.surface: A small piece of a road is managed by a motoring club.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the Automobile Association, a British breakdown and motoring club; 'arterial way' suggests a road but means a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's largest artery, the chief route for blood leaving the heart.

clue.text: Lady during month to perform in an exaggerated way

indicators.note: during puts the woman inside the month

parts.note: Oct is short for October
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman sometime in a certain month goes over the top in her acting.
explanation.definitionFit: To overact is to ham it up, playing a part too theatrically.

clue.text: One worrying runner

explanation.surface: A pest who keeps pestering is also out on the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who harries keeps harassing; and a cross-country athlete, or a hound hunting hares, is a runner.

clue.text: Debris or gold found in the state

indicators.note: found in puts the gold inside the state

parts.note: Maine is a US state
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Rubble, or perhaps gold, is discovered somewhere in the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Moraine is the rock and gravel debris carried and dropped by a glacier.

clue.text: Butter that is not from the plain?

definitions.text: Butter that is not from the plain?

parts.words: Butter that is not from the plain?
parts.note: read butter as one that butts with its horns, living up on the heights rather than the flat lowlands

explanation.surface: A spread that does not come from flat farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: A horned climbing animal of high rocky country butts, so it is a butter that lives far from the flatlands.
